doc.title: Daryl Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2024

title: Playing England and her UK Nooks and Crannies Tour
summary: She describes working Pizza on the Park, Pizza Express venues and small English and Welsh towns, building on Waldorf contacts.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Wow. No but I’ve had steady jobs, anonymous type jobs in restaurants where I would meet — ooh sorry — it’s meeting people and bonding in some cases. They become like best friends or kind of like family, and even traveling I got to go to England and started performing at Pizza on the Park in London, which was a place that Blossom Dearie played in and Dave Frishberg and lots of jazz people, some singers, and the ownership of that, let’s say the circle of places became The Pizza Express Live and they have a couple of other places in London where jazz musicians play, and one called The Pheasantry which is a little bit more singer-friendly so I’m going to be there in September. But during the ‘90s, when I had these recordings coming out on Arbors and things were still a little easier to travel, and they had more jazz societies around the country. Britain is, you know, they love, particularly trad jazz, although they have great musicians there for everything. But I started developing what I was calling my U.K. Nooks and Crannies Tour. And I prided myself on playing places that even Brits never heard of. How do like Clethorps, which is up north. Sounds like a prehistoric animal.

Or, I played, I’m going, in fact I’m going to be going back there in Wales there’s a lovely little area on the sea called Mumbles. And I met some of these people when they came to The Waldorf, and some have been enduring relationships.
